meta.title: How Customer-Driven Is Your Team? [Quiz]
meta.description: Take a quick quiz for product managers, researchers, and designers to see how much real customer insight drives your team’s roadmap, decisions, and…

hero.intro: Pick your role to get a score, a benchmark, and a clear picture of what the next level looks like for you.

cards.title: Are you a data-driven PM?
cards.text: Find out if your roadmap is driven by real customer signal—or gut feel and the loudest voice in the room.

cards.title: How impactful is your research?
cards.text: Discover whether your insights are actually influencing decisions—or getting buried in docs nobody reads.

cards.title: Are your designs customer-driven?
cards.text: See how connected your design process is to real customer insight—and where the gaps are costing you.

ctaFooter.h2: Turn customer feedback into product innovation

product.introHeading: Are you a data-driven product manager?

questions.text: Where does customer feedback live at your company?

options.text: Mostly in people’s heads and notes apps
Spread across Slack, email, Notion, and other tools
We have a dedicated tool, but not everyone uses it
One central place the whole team can access

questions.text: When a PM needs customer evidence for a roadmap decision, what happens?

options.text: They go from memory or ask around
They ping the research team and wait days or weeks
They dig through old Notion docs themselves
They search a shared repository and find something quickly

questions.text: How long does it typically take to synthesize a round of user interviews?

options.text: We don’t really synthesize—we just share raw notes
1–2 weeks of manual work
A few days with good tooling
Hours—AI handles most of the heavy lifting

questions.text: How does your team share research findings?

options.text: Verbally or in a long email nobody reads
A Notion doc that gets forgotten
A research report shared in Slack once
A living repository teammates can query anytime

questions.text: How often does customer feedback directly influence your roadmap?

options.text: Rarely—we move too fast for that
Occasionally, when research aligns with planning
Often, but it’s hard to prove the connection
Consistently—every initiative is tied to customer signal

questions.text: Which best describes your support and sales feedback loop?

options.text: Support and research teams don’t really talk
Someone forwards Zendesk tickets occasionally
We aggregate it, but analysis is slow
Feedback from support and sales flows into insights automatically

questions.text: How do you handle high-volume feedback—app reviews, NPS, support tickets?

options.text: We look at the numbers but not the actual comments
Someone reads a sample and reports themes manually
We tag and categorize it, but it takes significant time
It’s automatically classified and we get alerted to emerging trends

questions.text: How would a new PM find out what customers have said about a specific problem?

options.text: Ask around the office
Dig through Slack threads and docs for an hour
Find a research repo but struggle to navigate it
Search and get an answer in minutes

questions.text: How do you know if a customer pain point is getting worse over time?

options.text: When it starts showing up in churn interviews
When support tickets spike and someone flags it
We check manually on a regular cadence
We have automated monitoring that alerts us to trend shifts

questions.text: When leadership asks "what do customers think about X?", what happens?

options.text: Someone scrambles to pull together an answer
We surface a few relevant quotes and hope for the best
We have a decent answer but it takes a day to prepare
We point them to a dashboard or send a generated report in minutes

tiers.name: Instinct-Driven
tiers.tagline: You’re moving fast, but flying blind.
tiers.cost: Roadmaps that miss the mark. Churn that surprises you. Features built for the wrong people.
tiers.nextLevel: Teams at Level 2 start centralizing feedback in one place—so decisions are grounded in something real.

tiers.name: Feedback-Aware
tiers.tagline: You’re collecting. But it’s not turning into action.
tiers.cost: Hours of manual work. Insights that don’t reach the people who need them. Decisions made without the evidence that was sitting right there.
tiers.nextLevel: Level 3 teams have a real research process—but the leap to Level 4 is where insights start reaching everyone, fast.

tiers.name: Research-Powered
tiers.tagline: You have a process. But it doesn’t scale.
tiers.nextLevel: Level 4 teams share insights proactively across the whole org—not just with the people who asked.

tiers.name: Insight-Led
tiers.tagline: Strong foundation. Time to go further.
tiers.cost: Manual work that should be automated. Gaps in coverage for high-volume feedback. Insights that reach leadership too slowly.
tiers.nextLevel: Level 5 teams use AI agents to monitor feedback streams, generate reports automatically, and surface risks before they become problems.

tiers.name: Customer-Intelligent
tiers.tagline: Your whole company runs on customer signal.

ctaFooter.h2: Turn customer feedback into product innovation

research.introHeading: How impactful is your UX research practice?

questions.text: How long does it take to go from raw interview data to a shareable insight?

options.text: Weeks—transcription and synthesis alone take forever
1–2 weeks of solid manual effort
A few days with good tooling and templates
Hours—AI handles transcription and first-pass synthesis

questions.text: When a PM asks for research evidence during a planning meeting, what happens?

options.text: You promise to get back to them after you’ve had time to look
You recall a study from memory and hope it’s still relevant
You find something in your repo, but it takes time to navigate
You search your repository and surface the answer in minutes

questions.text: How do you currently handle transcription and note-taking after interviews?

options.text: Manually—it’s one of the most time-consuming parts of the job
Lightweight tools, but you’re still doing most of the analysis
Good tooling for transcription, but synthesis is still manual
Automated transcription with AI-assisted tagging and analysis

questions.text: How do research insights get discovered by people outside the research team?

options.text: They don’t, unless someone explicitly asks
We share a doc or report after each study
We have a repository, but people rarely explore it on their own
Insights are proactively surfaced and shared across teams

questions.text: How do you measure the impact of your research on product decisions?

options.text: We don’t—it’s hard to trace
Anecdotally—we notice when a study influenced a decision
We track which studies were cited in PRDs or roadmap decisions
We have dashboards that connect research to shipped features and outcomes

questions.text: How do you handle high-volume qualitative data—like 30+ interviews or thousands of survey responses?

options.text: We sample a subset and hope it’s representative
We manually read everything, which takes weeks
We use affinity mapping, but it’s still slow and labour-intensive
AI analyzes it all and surfaces themes we can dig into

questions.text: How often do you find yourself re-doing research that probably already exists somewhere?

options.text: Constantly—there’s no way to know what’s been done before
Sometimes—the knowledge exists but it’s hard to find
Occasionally—our repo helps but it’s incomplete
Rarely—our searchable system prevents duplication

questions.text: How do stakeholders typically engage with completed research?

options.text: They don’t—reports get sent and never read
They skim the summary slide and ask follow-up questions later
They read it when it’s directly relevant to a decision they’re making
They proactively explore our insights repository on their own

questions.text: When a product ships and underperforms, how involved is research in understanding why?

options.text: Not very—by the time we find out, the team has moved on
We do a post-launch study, but results come too late to course-correct
We monitor feedback channels and flag themes to the team
Research signals automatically surface post-launch issues in real time

questions.text: How confident are you that your research is influencing the most important product decisions?

options.text: Not confident—it’s hard to even get a seat at the table
Somewhat—research is considered but often overridden
Fairly confident—we’re consulted regularly on major decisions
Very confident—research is embedded in how the whole team decides

tiers.name: The Reactive Researcher
tiers.tagline: You’re doing real work. But it’s not landing.
tiers.nextLevel: Researchers at Level 2 start building methods and consistency—reducing the time from study to insight.

tiers.name: The Process-Builder
tiers.tagline: You have methods. But synthesis is still the bottleneck.
tiers.cost: Weeks lost to transcription and note-taking. Insights that reach stakeholders too late. A growing backlog you’ll never fully clear.

tiers.name: The Repository-Keeper
tiers.tagline: You’ve built infrastructure. Now you need reach.
tiers.cost: A repo only researchers use. Impact that’s hard to quantify. Time spent maintaining systems instead of running more studies.
tiers.nextLevel: Level 4 researchers are treated as strategic partners—their insights are actively sought out and shape major decisions.

tiers.name: The Strategic Partner
tiers.tagline: Research is valued. Now make it scale.
tiers.nextLevel: Level 5 researchers use AI to handle the scale problem—so they can focus on the work that actually requires human judgment.

tiers.name: The Intelligence Engine
tiers.tagline: Research is how your whole org makes decisions.

ctaFooter.h2: Turn customer feedback into product innovation

design.introHeading: Are your designs grounded in real customer insight?

questions.text: When you start a new design, how do you understand what customers actually need?

options.text: Intuition and past experience—I know the product well
I reference old research if I can find it
I work with a researcher on discovery before I start
I have instant access to a searchable library of current customer insights

questions.text: When a stakeholder pushes back on a design decision, how do you defend it?

options.text: By explaining my design rationale and aesthetic choices
By referencing a piece of customer feedback I remember
By pulling up a research report that supports the decision
By surfacing specific customer quotes, clips, or data from our insights repository

questions.text: How quickly can you validate a design concept with real customer feedback?

options.text: Weeks—setting up a study takes time and research team capacity
1–2 weeks, if research has bandwidth
A few days—we have efficient processes for rapid validation
Hours to days—we have continuous feedback streams and always-on research

questions.text: How do you stay informed about what customers are struggling with in the current product?

options.text: Support tickets that occasionally get shared with me
I join user calls occasionally and read Slack summaries
I have access to a research repo and check it when designing
Customer pain points are proactively surfaced to me through automated feedback analysis

questions.text: When a design ships and something isn’t working, how do you find out?

options.text: Someone mentions it in Slack or a meeting
We see it in analytics—but not why it’s happening
We monitor feedback channels and flag themes to the team
Automated systems surface it with customer context before it becomes a real problem

questions.text: How often do you design something that gets significantly reworked after user testing or launch?

options.text: Often—we find out what users actually need after we’ve built it
Sometimes—testing helps but we still miss things
Occasionally—our validation process catches most issues early
Rarely—we’re grounded in customer insight before we start designing

questions.text: How do you collaborate with your research team?

options.text: We work in silos—design and research don’t overlap much
I request studies when I need them and wait for results
We collaborate on projects, but the process is slower than ideal
Research and design are deeply integrated—insights flow into my work automatically

questions.text: How do you communicate the ’why’ behind your design decisions to product and engineering?

options.text: I explain my thinking in design reviews
I include a summary of relevant research in my design docs
I link to research reports and highlight relevant findings
I embed customer quotes, clips, and data directly into my design artifacts

questions.text: When working on a new feature, how much customer evidence do you have before you start?

options.text: Very little—we often design first and validate later
Some—I use what research is available, even if it’s dated
A decent amount—we usually run discovery research beforehand
A lot—I have access to a continuously updated picture of customer needs

questions.text: How confident are you that your designs are solving real customer problems?

options.text: Not very—it’s hard to know until something ships
Somewhat—we do some validation but it’s not always enough
Fairly—our process includes enough testing to feel confident
Very—every design is grounded in real, current customer insight

tiers.name: The Intuitive Designer
tiers.tagline: You’re talented. But you’re designing for a mental model.
tiers.cost: Designs that look great but miss the mark. Rework after user testing. Stakeholder debates that customer data could settle in minutes.
tiers.nextLevel: Designers at Level 2 start building customer validation into their process—even if it’s still reactive and ad-hoc.

tiers.name: The Feedback-Gatherer
tiers.tagline: You’re seeking validation. But it’s too late in the process.
tiers.nextLevel: Level 3 designers build insight into the early stages of design—not just as a final check before shipping.

tiers.name: The Evidence-Seeker
tiers.tagline: You want customer insight in your process. The tooling isn’t there yet.

tiers.name: The Insight-Led Designer
tiers.tagline: Customer evidence is core to how you design.
tiers.nextLevel: Level 5 designers have customer signal flowing into their work automatically—so they spend their time on judgment, not on finding evidence.

tiers.name: The Customer Advocate
tiers.tagline: You’re the bridge between customers and the product.

ctaFooter.h2: Turn customer feedback into product innovation
